```plato
//==
// # Color
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Colors - color arithmetic
//  - Named colors - the 141 CSS Color Module Level 4 / X11 names

library Colors
{
    //==
    // # Colors - color arithmetic
    //
    // Implementation bodies for `Color` (`color.types.plato`): the `INumerical`
    // obligations (IAdditive, IScalable, IInterpolatable, INumericalLimits), computed
    // component-wise over R/G/B/A including alpha. The 141 CSS/X11 named colors
    // follow in the next section.

    //==
    // Color - the INumerical obligations, component-wise over R/G/B/A.
    //
    // Alpha participates in the arithmetic like any other component. That is the
    // right behaviour for a linear-light value type (it makes Lerp a straight
    // 4-vector interpolation), but it is NOT alpha compositing
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_compositing): premultiplication and
    // Porter-Duff operators belong with the imaging package.

    // Component-wise sum, alpha included.
    Add(a: Color, b: Color): Color
        => (a.R + b.R, a.G + b.G, a.B + b.B, a.A + b.A);

    // Component-wise difference, alpha included.
    Subtract(a: Color, b: Color): Color
        => (a.R - b.R, a.G - b.G, a.B - b.B, a.A - b.A);

    // Component-wise negation. Meaningful as an additive inverse, not as a color.
    Negative(a: Color): Color
        => (-a.R, -a.G, -a.B, -a.A);

    // Component-wise linear interpolation in linear light; t is unclamped.
    Lerp(a: Color, b: Color, t: Number): Color
        => (a.R + (b.R - a.R) * t,
            a.G + (b.G - a.G) * t,
            a.B + (b.B - a.B) * t,
            a.A + (b.A - a.A) * t);

    // Scale every component, alpha included.
    Multiply(a: Color, scalar: Number): Color
        => (a.R * scalar, a.G * scalar, a.B * scalar, a.A * scalar);

    // Divide every component, alpha included. Precondition: scalar is non-zero.
    Divide(a: Color, scalar: Number): Color
        => (a.R / scalar, a.G / scalar, a.B / scalar, a.A / scalar);

    // Component-wise remainder against a scalar.
    Modulo(a: Color, scalar: Number): Color
        => (a.R.Modulo(scalar), a.G.Modulo(scalar), a.B.Modulo(scalar), a.A.Modulo(scalar));

    // The additive identity: transparent black.
    Zero(_: Color): Color
        => (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0);

    // The multiplicative unit: opaque white.
    One(_: Color): Color
        => (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0);

    // The component-wise least representable value.
    MinValue(_: Color): Color
        => (Number.MinValue, Number.MinValue, Number.MinValue, Number.MinValue);

    // The component-wise greatest representable value.
    MaxValue(_: Color): Color
        => (Number.MaxValue, Number.MaxValue, Number.MaxValue, Number.MaxValue);

    //==
    // # Color8

    // All four channels participate in the digest.
    Hash(self: Color8): Integer
        => ((self.R.Hash * 31 + self.G.Hash) * 31 + self.B.Hash) * 31 + self.A.Hash;

    //==
    // # ColorGradient
    //
    // Sampling a stop list. Stops are assumed ordered by Position; a parameter
    // before the first stop or after the last takes that stop's colour (clamped
    // ends, not wrapped), and two stops at the same position make a hard edge
    // rather than a division by zero.

    // The index of the last stop at or before the parameter, or 0 when the
    // parameter precedes every stop.
    StopIndexAt(self: ColorGradient, t: Number): Integer
        => self.Stops.Count.Range.Reduce(0, (acc, i) => self.Stops[i].Position <= t ? i : acc);

    // The blend between the bracketing stop pair. Precondition: at least one stop.
    GradientSample(self: ColorGradient, t: Number): Color {
        var index = self.StopIndexAt(t);
        var lower = self.Stops[index];
        var upper = self.Stops[(index + 1).Min(self.Stops.Count - 1)];
        var span = upper.Position - lower.Position;
        var local = span <= 0.0 ? 0.0 : ((t - lower.Position) / span).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        return lower.Color.Lerp(upper.Color, local);
    }

    // The colour of the gradient at the given parameter; transparent black when
    // the gradient carries no stops at all.
    ColorAtParameter(self: ColorGradient, t: Number): Color
        => self.Stops.Count == 0 ? Color(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0) : self.GradientSample(t);

    //==
    // # Named colors - the 141 CSS Color Module Level 4 / X11 names
    //
    // The named-color table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_colors): 141 CSS
    // Color Module Level 4 / X11 names as `Color8` constants. The `Color` arithmetic
    // is in the section above.
    //
    // COLOR SPACE - read before using the named colors. The CSS/X11 names are defined
    // as **8-bit sRGB** (gamma-encoded) values, so they are declared here on `Color8`,
    // whose doc comment already states it is "typically sRGB-encoded". They are NOT
    // `Color` values: `Color` is LINEAR-light RGBA, and NO transfer-function conversion
    // happens anywhere in this section. To obtain a linear `Color` from one of these
    // constants you must decode explicitly through the sRGB transfer function - the
    // `TransferFunction`/`ColorSRGB` vocabulary in `color-spaces.types.plato` owns that
    // conversion. Treating a Color8 constant as if it were linear light will visibly
    // wash out any blending, filtering, or lighting done with it.
    //
    // Alpha: the CSS/X11 table defines RGB only; every constant here is fully opaque
    // (A = 255).
    //
    // Constants follow the tree-wide idiom of dispatching on an ignored receiver of the
    // result type, so they read as `Color8.AliceBlue` (see `constants.library.plato`).

    //==
    // Values are 8-bit sRGB (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRGB), fully opaque.
    // Read as `Color8.CornflowerBlue`. Exact duplicates in the standard are
    // preserved as separate names (Aqua = Cyan, Fuchsia = Magenta) because both
    // spellings are in the spec.

    // sRGB (240, 248, 255), opaque.
    AliceBlue(_: Color8): Color8
        => (240, 248, 255, 255);

    // sRGB (250, 235, 215), opaque.
    AntiqueWhite(_: Color8): Color8
        => (250, 235, 215, 255);

    // sRGB (0, 255, 255), opaque.
    Aqua(_: Color8): Color8
        => (0, 255, 255, 255);

    // sRGB (127, 255, 212), opaque.
    Aquamarine(_: Color8): Color8
        => (127, 255, 212, 255);

    // sRGB (240, 255, 255), opaque.
    Azure(_: Color8): Color8
        => (240, 255, 255, 255);

    // sRGB (245, 245, 220), opaque.
    Beige(_: Color8): Color8
        => (245, 245, 220, 255);
```
